articles.title_orig: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
articles.title_zh: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
articles.content_orig:
It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation.
The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded.
The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Each of these companies has taken various lessons from SpaceX’s successful Falcon 9 rocket, arguably the most important of which is to build as much of one’s rocket, and particularly the engines, in-house as possible to control timelines and costs.
Now, with SpaceX pulling the Falcon 9 rocket from the commercial market as soon as 2028, the “race” to bring new medium-lift capacity into service is for more than bragging rights. There are fortunes to be made, and commercial space startups to be saved.
Satellite operators legitimately don’t know who to book launches with in the 2027 to 2030 timeframe because of uncertainty over which rockets will be available. The Falcon 9 is no longer for sale. The larger Vulcan and New Glenn rockets have stacked manifests and are expensive for small- and medium-sized satellites. And no one really knows which new medium-lift vehicles will be ready and capable of scaling up their launch cadence.
With all of this in mind, Ars Technica is here to help with a guide to the medium-lift space race in the United States, along with some (almost certainly wrong) predictions on when the rockets may debut. The list below is in our expected order of launch. Disagree? Feel free to shame us in the comments. And if you’re an engineer or technician working on one of these projects, keep going. This stuff is really hard and we salute your dedication. Prove us wrong!
The smallest of the medium-lift rockets under development, with a capacity of 3 tons in fully reusable mode and 7 tons in expendable mode, the Nova rocket is also arguably the most ambitious.
That’s because the rocket aims for full reusability, with a novel upper stage thruster design and heat shield to solve the difficult problem of protecting a vehicle reentering at orbital velocity. Additionally, the first-stage engines are full-flow staged combustion, which is ambitious for a first engine design.
Despite all of this, the rocket is making credible progress toward liftoff. The Nova rocket’s first stage is nearly complete at its factory in Kent, Washington. Last week Stoke shipped the second stage of Nova to its test site, and if hot-fire tests are successful it will move to the launch site. The launch complex at Cape Canaveral, Florida, is nearly complete.
Recently, for the first time, Stoke began to publicly talk about a date for Nova’s debut. The company is targeting “early” 2027 for launch. That’s probably optimistic, but we could see a late spring or summer debut.
Predicted launch debut : July 2027
Technically, this is not a medium-lift rocket. The company is advertising up to 33.5 metric tons to low-Earth orbit in fully expendable mode for Terran R. But new rockets rarely hit their advertised lift capacity early in their lifetime, and with a reusable first stage (which is necessary for the economics of Terran R to close), the lift capacity is closer to 20 metric tons.
Nevertheless, this is a large and ambitious project. And it was pretty much left for dead until former Google Chief Executive Eric Schmitt acquired the company a year and a half ago. Schmitt has injected much-needed funding into Relativity, and sources report that morale at the Long Beach, California-based company has improved significantly.
In recent months the company has reported some notable progress. It completed acceptance testing for all 13 of the Aeon R engines that will power its first stage, qualified the first stage structures, and is making progress on assembly of the first stage. Then, last Friday, the company said the Terran R’s second stage had successfully completed its first integrated hot fire test.
Stoke and Relativity are fairly close to one another in their development timelines. Relativity is ahead in second stage testing, but Stoke has a lead in launch site readiness. I am going to give the slight edge to the smaller rocket in terms of being ready for launch.
Predicted launch debut : September 2027
With a lift capacity of between 8.5 and 15 metric tons, depending on first stage reuse and landing site, Rocket Lab’s Neutron rocket slots somewhere in between Nova and Terran R.
For a long time it appeared as though Neutron would become the first new medium-lift rocket to debut since Antares, but the vehicle has had some teething pains: Rocket Lab has experienced some problems with the Archimedes engine , and more recently the company revealed some challenges with carbon-fiber domes.
The Neutron rocket’s first stage is the “largest pressurized structure ever made out of carbon composite,” Rocket Lab chief Peter Beck said this month. “Because of its scale, we’ve had to develop new out-of-autoclave processes to build Neutron, and this includes custom cure cycles for the very large pieces, like the forward and aft domes for the propellant tanks on Stage One.”
That doesn’t sound particularly easy. Given the lack of flight hardware in evidence, we’re not sure the company meets its latest launch target, which is now sometime in 2027.
Predicted launch debut : January 2028
We began this article with the Antares rocket, which was developed by Orbital Sciences. That company was later acquired by Northrop Grumman. A few years ago, seeking a home-grown alternative to Antares, Northrop announced a partnership with Firefly to co-develop the Eclipse rocket .
Firefly is developing the Miranda engines that will power Eclipse’s first stage, and this work appears to be progressing well. But there has been little public talk about development of the first and second stage hardware that will be built around the Miranda engine. Similar to Rocket Lab, Firefly and Northrop are also working with carbon-composite structures, so there may be some challenges there.
The partnership between Firefly, a new space company, and Northrop, a traditional space company, is also likely to produce some friction. It is difficult to make an educated guess on Eclipse because there is so much uncertainty about the rocket’s development. Typically, that means things aren’t going well or quickly. For now, we’re leaning toward pessimism.
Predicted launch debut : NET 2029

articles.title_orig: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in patient who arrived from Uganda
articles.title_zh: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in patient who arrived from Uganda
articles.content_orig:
Nigeria has recorded a case of Ebola in a female patient who travelled from Uganda in East Africa to Abuja, capital of the West African state.
Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the diagnosis had been confirmed by laboratory tests.
The patient is in isolation and receiving medical care after being admitted to a hospital in Abuja.
Health authorities have begun contact-tracing to prevent further spread, with 44 close contacts of the woman identified.
Nigeria, the first West African state to report a case linked to the current Ebola crisis in East Africa, successfully stopped a previous outbreak in 2014.
Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.
The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
The outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo, which began in May, has claimed at least 4,600 lives, with more than 9,500 cases recorded, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reports .
It was caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
Shortly after the outbreak was announced, it was also reported in Uganda, where at least two people died. Uganda declared itself free of the disease in August after its last patient was discharged.
The disease has also spread to Kenya, which has reported at least nine infections.
On Monday, the US advised its citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya because of health risks and raised its travel advisory level for the country.
Since the outbreak, Nigeria has stepped up disease surveillance, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control issuing public health advice to travellers.
The agency says travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete a health declaration form. Those arriving from other countries are currently exempt.
It has also urged travellers to remain vigilant and seek medical attention promptly if they develop symptoms of Ebola.
In 2014, Nigeria managed to beat an outbreak of Ebola which caused at least eight deaths.

articles.title_zh: Nearly $1 million worth of rare Pokemon and sports cards stolen from FedEx truck in Orange County heist, police say
articles.content_orig:
SANTA ANA, Calif. (KABC) -- Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards, including highly valued Pokémon cards, were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near an Orange County business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.
The theft is the latest in a string of heists involving Pokémon cards, which have exponentially increased in value in recent years.
The Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement on Tuesday that the heist occurred on Oct. 13 outside the Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) office in Santa Ana.
The hundreds of stolen cards are estimated to be worth a total of $963,000, according to police.
"However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined," according to the Santa Ana police statement.
The cards belong to collectors from across the country who submitted them to the PSA to be authenticated and graded.
Two full pallets of collectible cards were stolen, and some cards on a third pallet were also swiped when thieves broke into a FedEx truck, according to police.
"The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokémon cards," according to the police statement.
Thieves carve hole through drywall to steal high-value Pokémon cards from Anaheim shop
As of Tuesday, no arrests have been announced in the memorabilia rip-off. Police said the investigation is ongoing.
The theft was first reported by The Athletic, which cited police sources saying the the FedEx truck was broken into during the 60 to 90 minutes the driver was away from the parked vehicle.
"We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items. We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues," Collectors, the parent company of PSA, said in a statement to ABC News.
The company said it deactivated the certificates for the missing cards and has notified its "marketplace partners to be on the lookout for rare and serialized items."
"Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value," the company said. "We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset."
FedEx released a statement to ABC7, saying, "The security of our customers' shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation. Further questions should be referred to local investigators."
One victimized collector, known by his online handle, Sky-B Cards, issued a YouTube video statement , saying the 104 cards he submitted to PSA for grading were among the stolen items. He said he paid more than $8,000 to have the cards graded by PSA and that his cards were insured for more than $150,000.
"These were 104 cards that I've accumulated over two years," Sky-B Cards said in the YouTube video. "There are many irreplaceable cards in here that I will never see again, and honestly that's what hurts the most, outside of being absolutely financially destroyed here."
The heist is the latest in a string of thefts in Southern California and elsewhere in the country of highly valued Pokémon cards, highlighting what appears to be an ever-growing demand for merchandise from the popular childhood card game.
In February, thieves broke into a collectibles shop in Anaheim, by cutting a hole through the wall from a neighboring shop they also broke into, stealing tens of thousands of dollars worth of Pokémon cards.
Captured on video surveillance cameras, the three thieves were seen grabbing hundreds of trading cards and bolting from the shop in less than 10 minutes.
In April, thieves staged a smash-and-grab heist at Elite Sports Cards in Chicago, stealing $100,000 in Pokémon cards, the store owner told ABC Chicago station WLS.
In an interview in April, Jared Mast, president of Mast Wealth Management Group, which deals in alternative investments including collectibles like Pokémon cards, told ABC News the value of Pokémon cards has risen sharply in the past year.
"I would say, collectively, over the last 12 months, things have gone up anywhere from 200 to 300%," Mast said.
Mast explained that Pokémon card value has risen in three different waves over the last decade. First, in 2016, with the arrival of Pokémon Go, the popular mobile game based on the playing cards, and then again in 2019 and 2020, as a generation of celebrities like Logan Paul invested in the collectibles.
ABC News contributed to this report.

Microsoft is reportedly planning to launch an Xbox “next-generation handheld device” for the holiday season of 2027. The Xbox next-gen console, codename Project Helix, would then launch in the holidays of 2028, according to a new report from Fortune .
The report doesn’t make it clear whether the handheld would be made by a manufacturer like Asus, or by Microsoft itself. Xbox teamed up with Asus for its Xbox Ally devices, which ran a modified version of Windows 11 with an Xbox mode enabled. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has also described Project Helix as a “ family of devices ,” suggesting that Microsoft’s next Xbox console may not be just one piece of hardware.
Last year Microsoft and AMD announced a “strategic multi-year partnership” to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation console. It seems increasingly likely that this will include a range of “Xbox” devices, running on AMD’s new chips.
The regular next-generation Xbox console may not arrive until 2028, though. Fortune reports that Microsoft is currently projecting that its Xbox Project Helix console may cost “between $1,200 to $1,800” for consumers, unless Microsoft is willing to subsidize the cost of the hardware.
Microsoft’s Windows and Xbox teams have also reportedly clashed over what software will power the next-gen Xbox. That’s not terribly surprising given the two teams have clashed multiple times over the past 25 years of Xbox. It sounds like Xbox is now controlling the direction of the software on Helix, though.
The report also touches on the rumored changes to Xbox Game Pass. Last month rumors emerged that Microsoft was working on an overhaul to Game Pass that will create tiers with or without ads, much like Netflix and other streaming services. Fortune says Xbox is looking at including add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer. This would make Game Pass a lot more flexible, but it’s not clear what happens to day one games and the overall price of Game Pass.
One of Sharma’s first big moves as Xbox CEO was reversing the Game Pass price hikes , after she admitted internally that “Game Pass has become too expensive for players.” Xbox dropped future Call of Duty titles from day one on Game Pass, and brought prices back down for its subscription service.
Fortune also reports that Sharma is planning a fresh round of Xbox layoffs this month, followed by more in November and January.

DETROIT — General Motors narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its free cash flow expectations after beating Wall Street's third-quarter expectations.
The Detroit automaker also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion after GM completed a $6 billion share repurchase program that was announced in January. GM did not disclose a specific time to complete the program.
Despite the positive news, GM stock fell nearly 7% during trading Tuesday as the company's outlook missed Wall Street's expectations.
Wall Street analysts were mixed before the report on whether GM would raise its guidance Tuesday amid concerns of slowing sales and rising commodity costs. Analysts' expectations included a midpoint of $13.41 per share for the year compared with GM's new $13.25 per share midpoint, according to LSEG.
Several analysts in investor notes Tuesday said GM's third-quarter results were solid, but raised concerns about whether higher costs and pressures on vehicle pricing would limit earnings growth next year.
Here's how GM performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:
GM's new guidance includes adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $14.5 billion and $15.5 billion, or $12.75 to $13.75 adjusted earnings per share, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of between $11.5 billion and $12.5 billion.
That compares with its raised guidance from July that included adjusted EBIT of between $14 billion and $16 billion, or $12 to $14 adjusted EPS, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion.
"I think the market's been pretty consistent from what we've said all year," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told CNBC's Phil LeBeau . "Our fourth quarter's going to be down sequentially. ... I think the fact that we're able to hold our guidance in the face of that late inflationary pressure in the year is another sign of the GM team executing really well."
GM on Tuesday said it expects commodity inflation costs to be around $2 billion, which was the high end of its previous guidance. That includes higher costs for logistics and dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, chips that are impacting multiple industries .
While the inflationary costs were at the automaker's high end of guidance, GM said its gross tariff costs are expected to be at the low end of its expected $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion range. Warranty costs are expected to be at high end between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, GM said.
Jacobson said vehicle pricing is relatively flat as inflationary costs continue to increase. He said the company would assess where consumers are in the coming year when deciding if it should pass costs along by raising prices more than normal.
"GM is performing well, and we are working hard to continue our momentum despite growing inflationary pressures through strategic investments in new products and services, and through improved quality and operating efficiency," GM CEO Mary Barra said Tuesday in a letter to shareholders.
The automaker also said the costs of its pullback in all-electric vehicles announced last year were "substantially completed," saying it has recorded $11.2 billion in such charges since the second half of last year, including paying $4.6 billion of $7.4 billion in cash through the third quarter.
The company's net income attributed to stockholders was $3.3 billion during the third quarter, up roughly $2 billion from a year earlier.
GM's North American operations continued to lead the automaker's results, accounting for $3.6 billion of its $4.1 billion in adjusted EBIT results during the third quarter.
GM's 2025 third-quarter results included $48.59 billion in revenue, net income attributable to stockholders of $1.3 billion and earnings per share of $2.80 adjusted.

PyTorch is the popular open-source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no re-writing of their apps.
Amazon made a similar announcement Monday, when it released its own version of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. TorchNeuron allows AI apps to be ported to Amazon’s homegrown AI chip, Trainium, and to AWS with no rewriting. Amazon also said it going even further in its effort to loosen Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch. It is submitting code to the main PyTorch project that decouples various features from Nvidia’s chips, making it more open to any hardware by default.
Google may be one-upping Amazon in a few ways, however. It says it worked directly with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (maker of vLLM) RadixArk (maker of SGLang), and others to ensure that TorchTPU’s features and code libraries work well with these popular AI development tools, just as the original PyTorch does.
Plus the search giant has launched a dedicated tool, the TPU agent suite , to help developers move their apps to Google’s chips and cloud and fix errors along the way. It even updated its popular LiteRT tool, which runs AI on phones, laptops and embedded devices, to work better with PyTorch AI apps.
None of this means AI app developers will automatically ditch Nvidia’s hardware en masse just because they can now easily move to alternative chips and clouds. But Amazon and Google are clearly working to end Nvidia’s advantage.

OpenAI announced on Tuesday that users can now lock ChatGPT conversations to keep sensitive chats private when others may have access to their screen or device. Users can secure their locked chats with a four-digit PIN, or use Face ID or Touch ID on supported devices.
Unlike the app’s Temporary Chats, which provide a separate session that doesn’t appear in chat history, users can return to Locked Chats at any time.
The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.
The addition of locked chats adds a new layer of privacy to ChatGPT, as the app is increasingly used for personal conversations . Of course, while locking a chat can limit access, it doesn’t address concerns about how sensitive information is stored or handled.
OpenAI notes that locking a chat doesn’t create end-to-end encryption or a separate encrypted vault, change how long it retains the chat, remove information that ChatGPT remembered before a chat was locked, or change the “Improve the model for everyone” setting.
Once users lock a chat, it moves to a dedicated “Locked Chats” section, where it’s kept separate from regular chat history, pinned conversations, and chat search results.
With Memory enabled, Locked Chats has its own separate memory shared across conversations within the section. New messages sent after locking a chat can update that memory, but don’t update regular Memory. That means new information from locked chats won’t leak into regular chats.
OpenAI says resetting a PIN permanently deletes all locked chats, files, and other content protected by the previous PIN.
Additionally, the Locked Chats option isn’t available for temporary chats, archived chats, group chats, chats created from a shared link, chats with scheduled tasks, and chats with meeting recordings.
Locked Chats will be available to users on ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans. The company notes that the feature is not available on ChatGPT for Healthcare. The feature is starting to roll out on Tuesday, so it may not be live yet for all users.

articles.title_orig: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo
articles.title_zh: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo
articles.content_orig:
Apps that have not been rebuilt for iPhone Duo will appear in the center of its inner display, with empty space surrounding the window, according to Apple’s developer guidance. The foldable, which starts at $1,999, goes on sale October 23, 2026, and how your apps look on it depends on which version of Apple’s software development kit (SDK) each developer last built with.
Apple says in its iPhone Duo preparation guide for developers that “all apps will run on iPhone Duo.” Running and fitting the screen are two different things, though, and Apple splits apps into three groups.
iPhone Duo has two displays. The inner one is a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR panel at 1878 by 2670 pixels, and the outer one is 5.4 inches at 1398 by 2034 pixels, according to Apple’s spec page.
Set us as a preferred source and our Apple reporting ranks higher in your Google Search results and Discover feed — one tap, no account changes.
Apple tells developers that “Hardcoded screen sizes, fixed orientations, and device assumptions can break layouts, leading to stretched, clipped, or misplaced content.” The system also moves apps between the two displays: “Unfold it and your app expands to fill the inner display; fold it and your app returns to the outer display.” Apps that were only ever designed for a fixed iPhone screen were not built for that.
This is the group most people will notice. Apple says these apps “run on iPhone Duo, but won’t adapt to all layouts.” When the phone is open, “your app will appear in the center of the display, with empty space surrounding the window.”
On the outer display, the change is smaller. With the phone closed, “the outer display will show your app’s content to the left of the status bar and camera.”
The apps still work. You just will not get the full benefit of the larger screen until the developer ships an update.
Apple describes this as a middle step. Apps built with the iOS 27 SDK “resize to fill most of the inner display on iPhone Duo, but still avoid the status bar on the right edge.” Apple says this “provides an improved experience, as empty space is minimized.”
So an app recompiled with the iOS 27 tools uses most of the screen, with the right edge left to the status bar.
These are the apps Apple calls “optimized for iPhone Duo.” They “extend to use the full display, with toolbars and tab bars appearing vertically below the status bar.” Apple says this gives people “an optimal and consistent experience as they move across displays.”
That vertical bar layout is visible in Apple’s own product images, where apps like Slack place their navigation down the right side of the inner display.
Apple’s guidance also says that on the inner display, an app “should look like a natural extension of its iPad layout.”
iPhone Duo will ship running iOS 27.1, as we covered when Apple released the update . Developers get the matching tools in Xcode 27.1, which Apple says “adds development support for iPhone Duo” and includes an iPhone Duo simulator.
Apple has given buyers a simple signal. When a developer submits iPhone Duo screenshots in App Store Connect, the app’s App Store product page “will display a badge to let people know your app is optimized for iPhone Duo.”
That badge is the easiest way to check an app before or after you buy. Apple will also make Duo screenshots mandatory: “Starting April 2027, any apps or games submitted will need to include screenshots for iPhone Duo.” We have more on that requirement here .
Apple opened App Store submissions on October 5, 2026, telling developers they could submit “iPhone Duo optimized apps and games in App Store Connect today.”
If an app you use every day shows up as a centered window with empty space around it, it was most likely last built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier. It will keep working, and an update from its developer is what moves it to a full-screen layout.
Apple is pushing developers along with an app resizability skill in Xcode, which “scans your project” for layout problems and “suggests a fix,” along with iPhone Duo workshops and labs.
For multitasking, Apple says the inner display supports Split View and app switching, and that content “reacts as iPhone Duo folds, reorients when it’s turned to the side, and switches to the appropriate display when it’s flipped over.”

After removing dislike counts years ago, new UI tests at YouTube are making it harder to even using the dislike button at all.
In 2021, YouTube removed the dislike count as a way to “de-weaponize” the button – effort that had been ongoing for years – with YouTube even acknowledging that it was a decision that users might disagree with. Now, following similar changes to Shorts , YouTube appears to be testing further hiding the dislike button.
A report on Twitter/X highlighted by Neowin showcases YouTube hiding the dislike button under an overflow menu, hiding it from view despite the like button remaining front and center. This appears to be on the desktop website, though we couldn’t replicate the same behavior on our end.
It’s not the only case of this happening, though.
Over the past couple of weeks, reports on Reddit have seen the dislike button vanish, with another web user seeing a slightly different UI to the one above, but with the same result of offloading the button to an overflow menu alongside the “Report” button.
YouTube runs tests like this frequently, but given the same change was made to the dislike button on Shorts several months ago, it’s all but certain that the same will happen to standard videos.

articles.title_zh: China’s Long Shadow over Washington’s Russian Diesel Deal
articles.content_orig:
On October 9, the US Treasury issued General License 135 (GL135), authorizing transactions involving Russian-origin diesel until April 7, 2027. On October 13, just four days after GL135 was issued, a tanker transporting roughly 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low-sulfur diesel was en route from the Baltic port of Primorsk toward Morocco. The destination of this shipment was not coincidental either, with the African country having struggled to procure diesel and petrol since the start of the Iran war.
In this sense, GL135 changes the economic calculus for countries that have had to keep their energy ties with Moscow politically or commercially opaque in order to preserve their traditionally close relation with the US and avoid straining relations with the EU. Moreover, the Moroccan case suggests that international sanctions regimes may have limited leverage over third countries once the threat of US enforcement is removed . So, although many US allies were already importing fuel from Russia (Figure 1), GL135 will affect the steep discount and simplify the logistic arrangements that characterized those transactions.
Therefore, the likeliest near-term consequence of GL135 is rerouting barrels that might otherwise have gone elsewhere to US-aligned countries and, possibly, reducing the discount at which Russian diesel traded because of sanctions-related risks, although global supply barely budges . In other words, two seemingly contradictory outcomes can coexist: the pressure on regions struggling to source fuel may ease as diesel shipments from Russia become easier to arrange and reach more buyers, yet the global market balance changes little. Still, the less discussed question is whether easier access to Russian diesel may have been deemed necessary to weaken Chinaâs leverage over fuel-short buyers.
The origins of GL135 should be understood through the interaction between US domestic political pressure and global market imbalances. Indeed, US domestic politics may itself be partly a consequence of the global diesel supply shock, given that disruptions to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have contributed to US retail diesel prices reaching levels not seen since 2008. Nevertheless, the timing makes the domestic political dimension difficult to ignore: the move came weeks before the midterm elections, when high diesel prices had become a political liability for Republicans.
The geoeconomic rationale behind GL135 is potentially even more relevant, albeit less discussed. Over the summer, China helped cap oil prices by limiting its imports of crude and, given a supply shock is now hitting another market tightly linked to that for oil, one could have expected Beijing to help stabilize the global economy again. Not least because Chinese commercial inventories of middle distillates, a category including diesel and jet fuel, are down just 8.4% from October 2025 . However, Chinaâs willingness to mitigate the crude-supply shock correlated with a different set of market circumstances, not least the USâs ability to increase production to avoid domestic shocks and alleviate scarcity through its strategic reserves. Instead, this time China is prioritizing its energy security by shoring up its strategic reserves and by restricting and tightly managing diesel exports. As a result, Beijing commands enough refining capacity to â bail out the diesel marketâ and it has acquired new leverage over fuel-importing countries that are increasingly exposed to its supply decisions.

Meanwhile, the US has not increased its supply enough to help the Philippines , Morocco , Tunisia , and other allies struggling to secure enough fuel to keep their economy running (Figure 2). Not least because rising prices at home reflect the level of US commercial inventories of refined petroleum products, which are over 10 million barrels lower than last year and regional stocks are up to 32% below the 2021-25 seasonal average. Crucially, the US has got less leverage in the diesel market than for crude, where releases from the strategic reserves and increased output can readily materialize. Moreover, a rapid increase in domestic refining is unlikely given that US refineries are already operating close to the mid-90% in utilization and there is no idle capacity that can come online on short notice. Rather, declining stocks are chiefly due to the closure or conversion to biofuel of several refineries across the country partly motivated by âgreenâ policies. According to one estimate, seven major closures and conversions have removed roughly 1.235 million barrels per day of US refining capacity, more than 6.5% of the total, making external supply disruptions more consequential.
Seen in this context, GL135 appears not just as an electoral maneuver, but also as an effort to reduce Chinese leverage on global diesel supplies by allowing buyers facing prohibitive prices to tap more openly into Russiaâs exports. However, the move will not materially balance the global diesel balance because the binding constraint remains operational refining capacity. Moreover, Moscow does not appear able to release large quantities of diesel into the market, let alone enough to match the scale of Chinaâs reduced exports, given that Ukraine continues to carry out attacks on Russian refineries. Still, the case of Morocco offers an early indication that removing sanctions on Russian diesel may grant some US allies temporary relief from domestic and regional diesel shortages even if the global market imbalance is not corrected any time soon and Russian refining capacity does not recover .
Having settled the origins of GL135, the next question is who benefits from the rerouting of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of diesel to buyers in undersupplied fuel markets.
GL135 widens the set of eligible partners from which fuel can be imported by removing the sanction-risk associated with Russian-origin diesel. However, several analysts tend to agree that a mere reallocation of existing barrels cannot solve supply bottlenecks in the diesel market as effectively as a recovery in refinery output in the US and Russia, unblocking traffic through Hormuz, or a liberalization of Chinese diesel exports. So, the answer depends less on the number of Russian barrels being traded than on how the value of those sales is redistributed.
Given that global supply remains insufficient to balance an inelastic demand and even oil producers like Russia and the US have struggled to add refining capacity, as Russian diesel gets rerouted the main near-term effect may instead be a redistribution of profits. The main reason Russian producersâ revenues could grow in the short term is that the sanction risk likely translated into a discount on the sale price of diesel, as it has done for crude oil. These price cuts drove exportersâ netbacks down. To further complicate matters, Russian exporters do not typically pay for insurance and freight, since their oil and fuels are sold on âfree-on-boardâ (FOB) terms, yet the sellerâs netback can still be affected indirectly by changes in freight and insurance. Practically, buyersâ willingness and ability to pay can limit the sellersâ ability to pass freight and insurance costs through and reduce its netback. Hence, the extensive sanctions with which the G7 established for maritime service providers working with Russian oil companies, put further downward pressure on the latterâs netbacks.
In fact, while the product was being sold at a discount, freight cost rose to cover the so-called âshadow-fleet premiumâ that shippers demanded as compensation for the sanctions and compliance risks. So, as long as those sanctions were backed by the threat of US enforcement, including through tariffs , part of the margin that would otherwise have accrued to Russian sellers shifted to logistics operators and intermediaries.

articles.title_orig: China threatens retaliation if U.K. follows the EU on tariffs
articles.title_zh: China threatens retaliation if U.K. follows the EU on tariffs
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Beijing has threatened to retaliate if the U.K. raises tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, aligning with the European Union.
Responding to POLITICO’s story that Britain was looking to act in “lockstep” with the bloc to counter China’s market dominance in electric cars, a spokesperson from the Chinese Ministry of Commerce said : “If the U.K. insists on imposing restrictions on Chinese electric vehicles, China will resolutely retaliate and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese industries.”
The U.K. is currently working with its European partners to avoid a 10% electric vehicle tariff from the beginning of next year, when stricter rules of origin under the Brexit trade deal kick in.
The British government is also lobbying to be included in the EU’s Made in Europe policies, which give Brussels-made products preferential treatment in certain procurement projects.
U.K. Trade Minister Anas Sarwar told POLITICO on the sidelines of the German-British Business Summit at Mansion House last week that “the more that the U.K. and the EU work together and act in lockstep, the better it is for both the U.K. and the European Union.”
“The automotive sector and partnership remain strong, but do we have to grapple with the challenge that comes from rapid expansion in China? Of course we do,” he added.
China urged Britain to follow World Trade Organization rules and warned it against copying Brussels’ approach, arguing that tariffs on Chinese EVs would be discriminatory.
“China urges the U.K. to abide by WTO rules, think carefully, and not follow the European Union,” said the Chinese Ministry of Commerce spokesperson. “China will closely monitor the U.K.’s developments.”

articles.title_orig: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
articles.title_zh: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war
A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.
Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.
Using a satellite internet connection to circumvent a communications blackout, Wadi also said 47 other people were transported to the nearest town, al-Mujlad. A medical source, requesting anonymity for his safety, said 30 of them died from their injuries.
The medic said: “A total of 80 people were killed in the drone strike on al-Dibab, and another drone strike on al-Mujlad injured four who are currently being treated.”
Wadi said the drone struck twice, 10 minutes apart, “on a transport hub where people gather to travel back to their villages after the market day ends”.
The attack is one of the deadliest single strikes since war broke out in April 2023 when a power struggle between the Sudanese armed forces (SAF), headed by Gen Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo , erupted into violence in the capital, Khartoum.
The RSF-declared administration, known as Tasis, accused the army of carrying out Sunday’s strike. All of West Kordofan state is under RSF control.
Sudan has witnessed an escalation in the use of drones in the war. Between January and April, drone strikes accounted for at least 880 civilian deaths, more than 80% of all conflict-related civilian deaths in Sudan.
After drone strikes on a busy livestock market in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur state, on Friday, the SAF said they had killed RSF fighters, but the RSF accused the military of killing 30 civilians.
The fighting in Sudan has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced many more. It has been fuelled by foreign powers with vested interests who are supporting sides in the conflict.
Last week, Rosemary DiCarlo, the undersecretary-general for political and peacebuilding affairs at the UN, warned the security council that the conflict and humanitarian crisis was deteriorating “with no breakthrough on the horizon”.
She said: “They [the warring parties] are not moving closer to dialogue. On the contrary, they seem to believe that they can make greater gains on the battlefield and that continued external support will allow them to pursue their objectives by force.”
AFP contributed to this report

articles.title_orig: China-Laos air base could be another Southeast Asian forward outpost for Beijing
articles.title_zh: China-Laos air base could be another Southeast Asian forward outpost for Beijing
articles.content_orig:
A new joint military training facility in Laos could give Beijing a lasting foothold in mainland Southeast Asia even without an immediate boost to its combat power, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
Beijing and Vientiane opened a joint support and training center and an aviation academy at Ban Keun, about 50 kilometers north of the Lao capital, on Sept. 29. Beijing says the facility will train Lao air force pilots and it will be maintained by both countries.
The airfield, once complete, would be China’s second joint military outpost in Southeast Asia, after a Chinese-funded expansion of Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base opened in April of last year. The facility at Ream, despite its official designation as a dual-use facility, has seen a regular rotation of Chinese naval vessels.
The joint facility in Laos could allow China to deepen military ties, familiarize personnel with overseas operations and lay the groundwork for a larger presence, Joseph Kristanto, a research analyst at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, told RFA.
“Ultimately, I think the more important question is not simply whether Ban Keun could accommodate Chinese military aircraft, but whether Beijing intends to develop the facility into a sustained operational hub,” he said.
China’s Defense Ministry said in an announcement that the facility would be maintained by both countries and was “not directed against any third party.” It said its construction and use complied with domestic and international law and would strengthen military cooperation and support regional peace and stability.
Laos’ state news agency KPL reported that officials from both countries described the project at the opening ceremony as the product of cooperation based on mutual respect and equality. The facility would develop Lao military pilots’ practical skills, it said.
The KPL report also said both sides pledged to expand cooperation through joint training and exercises, personnel development and humanitarian assistance. Neither that report nor the Chinese announcement specified how many Chinese military personnel would work at Ban Keun, how long they would remain or the conditions governing Chinese aircraft deployments.
Satellite imagery analysis provided to RFA suggests some construction continued after the opening of the joint airfield. But its future military significance will depend on more than its physical completion, including the extent of Chinese access and the frequency and nature of activities there, Kristanto said.
China already operates military facilities on disputed features in the South China Sea. Ban Keun could extend its overseas presence inland, offering opportunities to build closer ties with the Lao military and gain experience operating from a foreign facility, he said.
The airfield’s immediate military advantages are less clear, analysts said. China has airbases in its own southern territory closer to the South China Sea, raising questions about what additional operations an inland facility in Laos would enable.
In satellite imagery of the airfield during its opening, eight aircraft are visible. Private satellite imagery analyst Jacob Bogle told RFA they were K-8, also known as JL-8, light attack and training aircraft.
Examining an Oct. 7 image, he identified what he thought was one remaining aircraft, while cautioning that the image was blurry. He suggested the others had likely moved into hangars, although their locations could not be established from that observation.
Bogle also identified what appeared to be workshops and temporary construction infrastructure beside the southern end of the runway.
“So while the runway and main buildings are completed, it looks like there is still some minor work that is being finished,” he said.
The imagery does not establish who owns or operates the aircraft. Both China and Laos operate the K-8 type, according to analysts cited by Reuters.
But a Lao military officer, while downplaying concerns over increased Chinese military presence in Southeast Asia, confirmed to RFA that at least some of the fighter jets at the facility are Chinese.
“It is a pilot training airport. A group of people are envious that Laos has a flight training center, yet Laos has never complained about neighboring countries hosting U.S. air bases,” said the officer on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to speak on such matters.
“When Laos built Ban Keun Airport for pilot training, some people overreacted. Naturally, Chinese officials brought their own fighter jets, given that it is a joint Lao-Chinese operation,” he said.
Bogle said it was too early to determine China’s future position at Ban Keun, but that the facility warranted monitoring.
Kristanto said operating combat aircraft from Laos would require substantial investment in fuel storage, maintenance facilities, munitions, air defense and other supporting infrastructure.
“At present, I see little evidence that Ban Keun offers a decisive operational advantage over China’s existing facilities,” he said.
Such limitations do not rule out a broader role in the future. Ban Keun could theoretically support intelligence gathering, surveillance, logistics or forward aircraft deployments if the necessary infrastructure and access arrangements were established, he said.
A sustained Chinese military presence in Laos could add another consideration for neighboring Vietnam, which already faces China across its northern land border and contests Beijing’s claims in the South China Sea.
China’s expansive maritime claims overlap with the exclusive economic zones of Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia. Vietnam also claims the Paracel and Spratly island groups, where competing sovereignty claims are distinct from disputes over rights to surrounding waters. China controls the Paracels, while several governments occupy features in the Spratlys.
In 2016, an international arbitral tribunal rejected China’s claims to the entire South China Sea based on its controversial nine-dash line, which surrounds the whole sea. This claim was seen to exceed what Beijing could legally claim under the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Beijing rejected the decision, and has continued to assert its claims over areas that are within the exclusive economic zones of the other claimants.
China has strengthened this position through island-building and military infrastructure, including runways, surveillance equipment and air defenses on occupied reefs. Those facilities support a wider maritime presence in waters where rival claimants seek to protect fishing grounds, energy resources and access to their outposts.
Ban Keun would introduce a different geographic consideration for Hanoi, potentially bringing Chinese military activity to its western side as well.
Bogle argued that facilities in Laos and Cambodia, together with China’s South China Sea bases, had effectively encircled Vietnam.
Kristanto was more cautious. Vietnam would have to account for the possibility of a Chinese military presence beyond its northern border and the South China Sea, he said, but Ban Keun’s inland location and China’s existing airbases limit its immediate operational value.
“For now, I would characterize Ban Keun as a potentially important strategic foothold rather than a major shift in the regional military balance.”
China’s involvement at Cambodia’s Ream naval base shows why a facility’s use over time can be more revealing than its designation as a joint training center, the analysts said.
China financed an expansion of Ream, on Cambodia’s southern coast, where its joint support and training center opened in April 2025. Cambodia maintains that Chinese personnel and warships are not permanently based there.
An analysis published in May 2025 by the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative documented Chinese naval vessels rotating through Ream after their initial arrival in December 2023.

articles.title_orig: If Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catch
articles.title_zh: If Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catch
articles.content_orig:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla had separately formed special committees to discuss the idea of a merger, taking a small step toward the possible consolidation of his two biggest companies.
Musk, who is the CEO of both companies, said that the special committees had not reached an agreement and that there was no guarantee they would. He said a merger would require support from both sets of shareholders.
“I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said.
Musk spoke about the potential tie-up during a call with Wall Street analysts about SpaceX’s quarterly results, which surpassed estimates; the company’s revenue more than doubled in part from renting out computing capacity to other artificial intelligence firms.
There has been intense speculation in the stock market over whether a combination might happen, and the two companies already overlap in some areas, including semiconductor manufacturing . In January, Tesla announced that it was investing about $2 billion to acquire shares in an AI startup that’s a subsidiary of SpaceX.
Musk said that, because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations, he is not a member of either special committee or involved in the talks. He said the committees consist of the two boards’ independent directors but did not specify the memberships.
“It’s an odd Kabuki dance, where groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation,” he said during the earnings calls. He also said that even answering a question about the idea from an analyst felt like “dancing through a minefield.”
Musk, though, endorsed the idea.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies, as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating,” he said. He mentioned several areas of current or potential future cooperation, including AI software development, chip design and robotics.
Musk has already consolidated some of his other holdings. Last year, he merged his social media company, X, with his AI startup, called at the time xAI. Then, in February, SpaceX acquired xAI , which Musk has since renamed SpaceXSI.
David Ingram is a tech reporter for NBC News.

Edited by Manish Pandey and Matt Spivey
Paul Adams Diplomatic correspondent
After a torrid ten days, dominated by evidence of another breakdown in relations between Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump, the tone in Oslo seemed curiously upbeat.
The Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re, said he was glad to have been able to "straighten out a few things" (adding that there was "nothing to gainâ¦from digging into what was said yesterday").
President Zelensky seemed especially pleased with the outcome of a morning conversation with the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio.
The crucial issues of early warning of Russiaâs ballistic missile strikes had, he suggested, been resolved.
The two men had also discussed Ukraineâs access to Patriot interceptor missiles and Elon Muskâs Starlink system, both vital for Ukraine. Zelensky said he expected "good results".
Finlandâs president, Alexander Stubb, said it had been "a good day for peace", with plenty of progress made "under the radar" on substantive and technical issues.
Steve Witkoff is taking an updated set of proposals to St Petersburg to find out what Vladimir Putin thinks. How long this optimistic moment lasts is anyoneâs guess.
We're now ending our live coverage, but you can keep up to date in our news story.
Bernd Debusmann Jr White House reporter
Trump and Zelensky have had a difficult, up-and-down relationship since the US president came back to the White House, most notably during their tense, fiery meeting in the Oval Office last year.
Their relationship, however, has taken a notable turn over the last few weeks.
It has become increasingly clear that in Trump's eyes, Zelensky is to blame for the ongoing war. A little over a week ago, Trump went as far as to say that Ukraine needs a "new president" to replace him.
We heard more of that today, with Trump saying that the US wants Zelensky to "make a deal" and should have done so already.
He also questioned US support for Ukraine, telling reporters that the US has gotten "absolutely nothing back" for its support "except grief, death and tremendous monetary loss".
Notably, his comments came on the same day Zelensky met with Steve Witkoff and other US representatives in Oslo.
During a news conference, Zelensky said he is "ready for negotiations" and called for trilateral talks with the US and Russia.
Trump's comments will no doubt cause alarm in Kyiv and in European capitals.
It will also sounds alarm in the offices of Washington lawmakers - both Democrats and Republicans - who feel strongly that the US should support Ukraine and who have publicly questioned Trump's policies towards Russia - including his recent waiver on punishing sanctions meant to compel Moscow to come to the table.
Trump was asked by a reporter in the Oval Office about the war in Ukraine
We have just heard from US President Donald Trump, who says the US has given "tremendous" amounts to Ukraine but received nothing back in return.
Speaking from the Oval Office, following an announcement about fraud, the US president says it is time for Ukraine to end the war.
He describes the hatred between Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky as being "tremendous", saying this may be the reason they have been unable to reach a deal.
"We've given a lot to Ukraine. We've gotten absolutely nothing back except grief, death, tremendous monetary loss," Trump says.
As we reported earlier, President Zelensky said in the press conference that he is "thankful" to the US as intelligence on Russian strikes "works now".
Zelensky's adviser Serhii Beskrestnov last week told the BBC that lives had been lost in Ukraine because Kyiv was at the time not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks.
White House officials have said there were no changes to intelligence sharing operations between the two countries.
Earlier today, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected as "scandalous" accusations that Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding intelligence.
Zelensky told reporters this evening that the early warning systems are important to the Ukrainian people and children as it shows when attacks are incoming.
Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks
Zelensky also said restrictions on Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing. He earlier said speed limits had been imposed on Starlink terminals, and that Kyiv had not been told about this in advance.

articles.title_orig: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.title_zh: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.content_orig:
Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.
As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.
The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.
“This will be a massive cleanup job, bigger than Heartbleed,” Filippo Valsorda, a cryptography engineer and a cryptography maintainer for the open source Go programming language, told Ars. “There will be a very, very long tail, IoT devices, Docker containers, forgotten Linux machines, unmaintained CLI tools that shipped their own copy of the roots (which is common in some ecosystems, like Python). Also, Linux distributions are still rolling out updates, some of them are not ready yet, and then system administrators will need to apply them to a lot of machines.”
Heartbleed is the name of a critical vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptography library. In 2014, it came under mass exploitation . Exploits let many unaffiliated hackers decrypt TLS-protected exchanges between parties. They also recovered private TLS certificate keys, session cookies, and passwords. The attacks compromised thousands of servers, some belonging to large companies and government agencies around the world.
Recovery required a long series of steps that took years. Steps included patching OpenSSL on all affected devices, reissuing millions of TLS keys, revoking old certificates, rotating passwords and session tokens and updating embedded devices and other forgotten systems—something that was extremely time- and resource-intensive, especially at Internet scale.
“Every time you need a lot of different people in different contexts to do something, it will take a long time,” Valsorda explained. “This time it’s worse because there’s more contexts, more people, and more heterogeneity.”
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2 384 , or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
As noted, most browsers have already blocked the intermediate certificates. The exception appears to be Edge, which at the time this article went live was still connecting to 12 vulnerable hosts. In response to questions asking why and if the company has plans to do so, a Microsoft representative the company will be in touch if it has anything to “share.” Meanwhile, Signal, WhatsApp, Wireguard, and other apps that don’t rely on TLS for confidentiality aren’t affected. This page and the emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com site show apps known to be patched so far.
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest link, which in this case was eMudhra. Fortunately, transparency logs account for much of that failure, but this measure requires parties to actively monitor massive feeds and works only after unauthorized certificates have been issued. eMudhra representatives weren’t immediately available to answer questions.
One caveat: exploiting compromised certificates requires an active adversary-in-the-middle attack, meaning the attacker must act as a proxy between two TLS parties and receive encrypted traffic, decrypt it, reencrypt it, and send it to the other party. Such capabilities, in some cases, are usually limited to only the most well-resourced attackers. People with control of a local network—at a coffee shop, university, or other organization—face much less of a challenge.

articles.title_orig: China built more than twice naval tonnage of US in 2024-25: Euronaval
articles.title_zh: China built more than twice naval tonnage of US in 2024-25: Euronaval
articles.content_orig:
PARIS — China built more than twice the naval tonnage of the United States in the 2024-25 period, narrowing the gap between the two countries’ navies, according to the World Defense Shipbuilding report published by Euronaval ahead of the 2026 edition of the naval defense show.
The combined tonnage of combat ships built by China in the two years through to December 2025 amounted to 636,208 tons, compared to 270,509 tons for the United States, according to data compiled by Flottes de Combat and French maritime industry association Gican.
China accounted for more than a third of the global naval tonnage constructed in 2024-25, based on the Euronaval report. U.S. lawmakers and congressional researchers have warned that China’s greater shipbuilding capacity, combined with delays and bottlenecks in U.S. naval shipbuilding, could hurt America’s ability to keep up with Beijing’s expanding fleet.
“We are seeing a fairly substantial expansion of naval forces, and consequently of shipbuilding,” said Philippe Missoffe, the general director of Gican, in a press briefing here on Tuesday. “We’re seeing an increase in power capabilities, particularly nuclear-powered attack submarines for example.”
Global naval construction overall was booming in the period, with 1.47 million tons of combat vessels built in 2024-25, compared with 959,671 tons in the prior two years. The value of global naval construction amounted to $123.9 billion, climbing from $81.8 billion in 2022-23.
The value of Chinese combat-vessel construction was US$43.5 billion in the latest two-year period, compared with $26.8 billion for the U.S., the report said.
China has reversed roles from 2022-2023, when production of the country’s naval yards amounted to 202,520 tons, compared with 245,703 tons for the U.S., according to the previous edition of the shipbuilding report published in 2024.
The U.S. fleet of combat vessels of more than 200 tons amounted to 3.11 million tons as of Jan. 1, 2026, compared to 1.44 million tons for China’s fleet, the report showed, That compares with 3.22 million tons for the U.S. and 1.3 million tons for China two years earlier.
Russia was in third place in terms of naval construction in 2024-25, with 149,056 tons built, followed by India with 76,430 tons and Italy with 53,700 tons. Turkey, France, Japan, South Korean and Romania rounded out the top 10 of naval builders.
The four-day Euronaval show, the world’s biggest maritime-defense exhibition, is set to kick of in Paris on Nov. 3. The number of exhibitors will be more than 40% higher than in 2024, according to the organizers.
Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.

articles.content_orig:
Walmart on Tuesday debuted a discounted joint membership with Sam's Club, the retailer's warehouse club, in a bid to attract inflation-weary customers.
Walmart said it's offering a combined Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership for $120 a year, saving shoppers who buy them individually about $100 annually, according to the company.
The joint membership gives customers access to members-only discounted prices at Sam's Club, free delivery on goods from both retailers, a Peacock or Paramount+ subscription plan, 10 cents off on gas at 17,000 stations across the U.S. and rewards on eligible purchases (Paramount+ is owned by Skydance, which also owns CBS News).
"For $120 a year, we're raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own," Walmart CEO John Furner said in a statement.
Existing members can also upgrade their plans. Walmart+ members can switch to the dual membership for $22 more per year, while Club members can upgrade to Sam's Club Plus for $60 more per year, which includes Walmart+.
Walmart is betting that low prices and discounts will draw cash-strapped Americans into its stores. In August, Chief Financial Officer John Rainey announced price cuts across a range of products, including food.
"We're investing heavily in price because customers need us to and because we believe it drives market share gains over time," Rainey said at the time.
Walmart's efforts to ease prices come as consumers continue to grapple with elevated inflation, with the Consumer Price Index rising at an annual rate of 3.7% in September .
After five years of elevated inflation, nine in 10 Americans say prices are the most important factor shaping their economic outlook, according to a recent CBS News poll.

Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.
As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.
The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.
One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.
We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.
Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.
This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.
In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.

The Government Service Network (GSN) reported a surge of 185.6 million cyberattacks in July, suggesting that Beijing could be preparing large-scale interference operations ahead of the Nov. 28 elections, government officials said.
Cyberattacks on the network, likely originating in China, spiked between June and last month, the National Security Bureau (NSB) said in a report submitted to the Legislative Yuan for a meeting scheduled for tomorrow.
As of last month, the GSN was attacked 2.58 million times a day on average, and the attacks reported in July exceeded the sum of total cyberattacks in the first quarter this year, the document said.
Cyberattacks exceeded 100 million in three months last year: during the anniversary of President William Lai’s (賴清德) inauguration in April (100 million), in May (about 300 million) and during Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim’s (蕭美琴) visit to Europe in November (about 200 million), it said.
The NSB cannot rule out the possibility that the July attacks are part of Beijing’s plan to meddle in next month’s nine-in-one elections, the report said, adding that the agency had warned of the same in April.
Chinese hackers in the first half of the year targeted academic institutions, telecommunications and defense industry supply chains as part of a long war against Taiwan’s critical infrastructure, it said.
The attacks were aimed at disrupting Taiwan’s ability to govern and direct national defense policy, its collaboration with other governments and the theft of sensitive technology, it said.
Beijing-directed cyberwarfare continues to improve in sophistication and artificial intelligence (AI) technology has been deployed in hacks, it said.
AI is utilized across various stages of a cyberattack, including probing for weaknesses, target seeking, searching for zero-day exploits and malware attacks via e-mail, the report said.
Automation has increased Chinese hackers’ operational tempo and their efficiency in finding gaps in Taiwan’s defenses and identifying targets for infiltration, it said.
Meanwhile, the NSB said it believes that Beijing would leverage technology and human intelligence to craft a strategy to influence next month’s elections, targeting Taiwan’s domestic wedge issues such as energy, food safety and national defense, and using fake polls and reports about the races, and AI-generated content, it said.
Suspicious social media accounts made 2.5 million posts containing controversial or disputed information from January to last month, up 48 percent compared with 1.69 million in the same period last year, the report said.
The method and platform for spreading cognitive warfare posts included content farms, AI-generated video or audio content, and brigading the comment section on platforms, forums and other Web sites, it said.
Facebook and Threads accounted for 68.9 percent and 9 percent respectively of all controversial content from suspicious accounts, it said.
Suspicious posts on Facebook and Threads were up by 25.3 and 4.5 percentage points from last year respectively, indicating China’s increasing preference for using these platforms, the report said.
AI is playing an increasingly prominent role in Beijing’s informational operations, it said.
China’s strategy for manipulating Taiwanese public opinion follows the model of using official outlets to craft narratives, which are then amplified by troll, bot and public relations company-owned accounts, the report said.

articles.title_orig: Trump Tariffs on Canada Spark Latest Lawsuit Over Trade Powers
articles.title_zh: Trump Tariffs on Canada Spark Latest Lawsuit Over Trade Powers
articles.content_orig:
A new lawsuit filed Tuesday challenges President Donald Trump 's invocation of a Depression-era law to impose 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian goods .
Trump in July used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to slap those steep tariffs on Canadian hockey sticks, wine, honey, wigs, and other products in response to alleged trade discrimination by Ottawa. It was the first time the 96-year-old law had ever been used to impose a tariff.
"Section 338 is a relic of the retaliation-based tariff policy" that has been "impliedly repealed" by subsequent legislation, the civil complaint filed in the U.S. Court of International Trade says.
The suit was filed by Gellert Global Group, a New Jersey-based food importer that says its cheeses are covered by the tariffs. The complaint asks the court to declare the tariffs unlawful, block their enforcement, and order the Trump administration to issue refunds for duties already paid, with interest.
Gellert Global is represented by the Liberty Justice Center, the same legal group that dealt a major blow to Trump's trade agenda by successfully contesting his "reciprocal" tariffs.
The Supreme Court struck those tariffs down in February. The administration is in the process of refunding the estimated $166 billion that the federal government collected from importers through the reciprocal duties.
The Liberty Justice Center is currently engaged in two other lawsuits against what it says is Trump's misuse of laws to impose sweeping tariffs.
"This case is not about the president. It is about the presidency," the group's CEO Sara Albrecht said in a statement Tuesday morning announcing Gellert Global's suit. "No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required."
The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on the suit.

articles.title_orig: You Should Probably Check Your Google Home Speaker’s Data Usage
articles.title_zh: You Should Probably Check Your Google Home Speaker’s Data Usage
articles.content_orig:
The new Google Home Speaker has an issue where it downloads hundreds of gigabytes of data in the background for some owners.
Over the past week, several reports have emerged about how the Google Home Speaker appears to be continuously downloading data from company servers.
In my case, a Google Home Speaker that has not been used in the past day for voice commands or media streaming consumed 17 GB of data in 24 hours. At 3 a.m. PT, it downloaded 9.99 GB. Given the timing, this could be related to failed attempts to download device firmware.
Meanwhile, on October 13, the same speaker downloaded 41 GB of data. Over the past 30 days, the total download comes in at 132 GB.
It’s not clear if this is a widespread issue. Another lightly used Home Speaker of ours (in a different household) downloaded only 2 GB of data in the past month.
That doesn't make sense how much storage does it have? It's just downloading and deleting constantly?
Most routers let you check how much data a particular device has used. If you’re using Nest Wifi, go to the Google Home app’s Wifi top tab > Devices > select your speaker > Device usage graphs. You can switch between 1-, 7-, and 30-day graphs.
We’re not seeing this download issue with other Google Home and Nest devices, including several Nest Hubs in the same house as the affected Home Speaker.
If you have multiple Home Speakers and a limited data plan, this issue could easily breach your cap, as some have found.
In a statement to 9to5Google today, the company acknowledged the issue and said “a fix is already rolling out that should address this for users.”

Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans.
Nationwide, 14.5% of homes fell out of contract in September, according to Redfin data, the highest share on record apart from the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic.
